attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, in his voice. They are not quoted from anyone else.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' language, so it is scored. The trigger, a hyperscaler pulling out or debt stopping, comes from his rhetorical questions and is kept. 'AI was a sales pitch' slightly compresses 'conflated a great sales pitch with a thriving industry', but it is faithful enough. No deadline is given.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. A trigger needs a material retreat or a broad financing interruption, and harm must reach both broad markets and the real economy. It imposes no invented deadline or threshold. Because the scale of the trigger is undefined, the interpretation does decide when the claim resolves.

evidence.note: Secondary transcript of Microsoft's 2026-10-28 earnings call. It puts lower calendar-year capex down to third-party capacity delays, not a strategic retreat. That does not establish the trigger.

SpaceX's own 2026-10-26 announcement of a committed ~$40B GPU financing deal. It shows financing still available to one major builder, though closing is still pending. This is a company statement about itself, so it speaks to the trigger condition only.

IT Pro report, 2026-10-26, of Musk's claim that debt markets have largely shut off for neoclouds. This is one market participant's characterisation, not lending records. It does not establish a broad financing stoppage or any market or economic harm.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm conditional forecast with no deadline. The packet shows no qualifying hyperscaler retreat: Microsoft's capex change is tied to capacity delays. It also shows no corroborated broad financing interruption: there is only Musk's claim, and new large financings continue. With the trigger not established, the forecast cannot be scored. The packet also shows no market and economic harm attributable to such a trigger, and nothing rules it out.
